title: Diffusion model
reading: The slide introduces diffusion models by analogy to autoregressive models run in reverse: starting from a complete image and successively removing pixels, a process called signal corruption. It then contrasts this with the actual diffusion mechanism, which corrupts by adding noise (most commonly isotropic Gaussian) to produce progressively noisier signals, with the per-step update given in a boxed equation. Two horizontal filmstrips illustrate the reverse autoregressive sequence and the forward diffusion process.

visuals.description: Top filmstrip labelled 'Reverse autoregressive sequence': a pixel-art bird image progressively blacked out row by row until the frame is entirely black, with ellipses between groups.
visuals.assertion: Autoregressive generation reversed amounts to deleting pixels one at a time until nothing remains.

visuals.description: Red-boxed equations: x_t = sqrt(1-beta_t) x_{t-1} + sqrt(beta_t) eps_t, with eps_t ~ N(0, I).
visuals.assertion: Each forward diffusion step rescales the previous sample and adds isotropic Gaussian noise with variance beta_t.

visuals.description: Bottom filmstrip labelled 'Forward diffusion process': the same bird image degrades across eight frames into colourful random noise.
visuals.assertion: Repeated Gaussian noise addition drives a clean image toward pure noise.

concepts.name: Signal corruption
concepts.why_it_matters: Frames diffusion's forward direction as progressive destruction of information.

concepts.name: Forward diffusion process
concepts.why_it_matters: Defines the noising schedule that the model later learns to invert.

concepts.name: Isotropic Gaussian noise
concepts.why_it_matters: Standard noise choice making the forward kernel analytically tractable.

concepts.name: Autoregressive model
concepts.why_it_matters: Provides the comparison baseline for the pixel-removal analogy.

verbatim_spans: Diffusion model: adding noise to produce a noisier signal
